_readme: Provenance record for the 9 third-party skill packs fetch-vendor-plugins.sh builds at Docker build time (and locally, on demand). This file is tracked in git; the fetched plugin content it describes is NOT (see .gitignore) -- fetch-vendor-plugins.sh is the single source of truth for reproducing it, this file is the human-readable record of what was decided and why. destDir/wrapper/stripped_paths/extra_files/patches describe exactly what the script does for each entry; they are not machine-parsed by the script (nine fixed plugins do not earn a generic JSON-driven config reader in the Dockerfile's minimal `fetch` build stage) -- keep them in sync with the script by hand when either changes. The `skipped` array records plugins that were EVALUATED and deliberately not vendored, with why -- so the decision is not re-litigated from scratch next time someone asks.

vendored.name: superpowers
vendored.notes: All 14 skills copied verbatim with the repo's own .claude-plugin/{plugin,marketplace}.json. hooks/, assets/, docs/, scripts/, tests/, and other-platform (.codex-plugin/, .cursor-plugin/, etc.) directories are top-level repo dirs, siblings of skills/ -- excluded automatically by sourcePath scoping alone, no stripping needed within skills/ itself (verified against a real clone at the pinned sha: byte-identical).

vendored.name: ponytail
vendored.notes: Source repo has no .claude-plugin/plugin.json (uses a root-level plugin.json + plugin.yaml for a different, multi-platform packaging convention) -- the wrapper here is authored fresh (small enough to check into git directly, not vendored/fetched). commands/ (TOML format, not Claude Code's .md convention) and hooks/ were not vendored -- unvalidated mechanisms; the plugin_directories -> skill-loading path is what Phase A0 actually confirmed works. ponytail-mcp/ (a bundled MCP server) was also not vendored -- flagged as a future enhancement, not validated here. Verified against a real clone at the pinned sha: skills/ content is byte-identical.

vendored.name: caveman
vendored.notes: Only the caveman skill itself was vendored, per explicit direction -- the source repo is a large monorepo (browser extension, proxy server, compression engine, MCP server, multiple other caveman-* skills). LICENSING.md confirms skills/ is MIT while the engine/proxy/browse/mcp components are BSL-1.1 -- vendoring only the skill keeps this cleanly within the MIT-licensed surface. No .claude-plugin/plugin.json in source; wrapper authored fresh, same reasoning as ponytail. Verified against a real clone at the pinned sha: byte-identical.

vendored.name: security-review
vendored.notes: Skill + its references/ subfolder (bundled reference docs, a legitimate skill component) copied verbatim. No .claude-plugin/plugin.json in source (it's one skill among many in a shared collection repo); wrapper authored fresh. Verified against a real clone at the pinned sha: byte-identical.

vendored.name: impeccable

patches.reason: Every reference/*.md and SKILL.md names its own scripts via a hardcoded fallback path -- Copilot CLI does not reliably report a skill's base directory the way Claude Code does, so the fallback must resolve to where this image actually places the skill.
Removes the just-stripped `live` command from the argument-hint token list.

patches.find: | `live` | Iterate | Visual variant mode: pick elements in the browser, generate alternatives | [reference/live.md](reference/live.md) |
patches.reason: Removes the Commands table row pointing at the stripped reference/live.md.

patches.find: **Hooks:** `/impeccable hooks <on|off|status|ignore-rule|ignore-file|ignore-value|reset>` manages the design detector hook for this project (auto-runs the detector after UI file edits and surfaces findings). Load [reference/hooks.md](reference/hooks.md) when the user invokes it with any argument.
patches.reason: Removes the paragraph describing the stripped hooks system.

vendored.notes: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE + NOTICE.md copied to the plugin root per Apache attribution requirement -- see extra_files above). Source repo ships an official Claude plugin at plugin/ (v4.1.1); its .claude-plugin/plugin.json and skills/impeccable payload copied. Stripped as interactive/unvalidated in a headless pipeline: the .grok-plugin (other-platform) directory, the four impeccable-* subagents, the hooks system, and the whole 'live' visual-iteration feature (server, browser injection, per-framework adapters) -- see stripped_paths above. The SKILL.md rows/paragraphs referencing the stripped features are removed so no instruction points at a missing file -- see patches above. Every '.claude/skills/impeccable' script-path fallback in SKILL.md and reference/*.md is rewritten to the absolute in-container path. scripts/ (everything not stripped) is left byte-identical -- they resolve their own paths relative to the module. Used by graph.py's UI-repo-gated prompt segments: shape (P3, methodology only), design rules + document (P6), critique (P11a), audit detectors + polish (P11b). All of the above verified against a real clone at the pinned sha via fetch-vendor-plugins.sh, diffed byte-for-byte against what was previously committed.

vendored.name: frontend-design
vendored.notes: One skill (skills/frontend-design/SKILL.md), ships its own .claude-plugin/plugin.json and LICENSE (Apache-2.0) inside the plugin dir -- copied verbatim, no curation needed. Prompt-encouraged (UI repos only) at minimal-code-to-green via graph.py's FRONTEND_DESIGN_SEGMENT, alongside the impeccable segments.

vendored.name: code-review
vendored.notes: One model-invocable command (commands/code-review.md, disable-model-invocation: false). CAUTION: the command body is GitHub-PR-centric (allowed-tools all Bash(gh pr ...) forms, aborts without an open PR) and fans out ~10 subagents (5 parallel Sonnet reviewers + Haiku scorers) -- real token cost. The CLI's own BUILT-IN code-review skill is preferred for the minimal-code-to-green requirement if the container spike shows it is model-invocable headless; this vendored plugin is the fallback and exists mainly for local-parity with the team's plugin set.

vendored.name: code-simplifier
vendored.notes: One agent (agents/code-simplifier.md) with frontmatter `model: opus` -- every invocation runs on Opus, a real per-remediation cost bump, accepted and scoped by the remediation prompt to flagged files only. Launched via the Task tool (requires builtin:task in the stage's available_tools -- see claude_chat_model._TOOL_NAME_MAP). The CLI's own BUILT-IN simplify skill is preferred for the remediation requirement if the spike shows it is model-invocable headless; the agent is the fallback.

vendored.name: mattpocock-skills

patches.reason: Upstream marks user-invoked skills non-model-invocable -- correct for a human-driven chat, fatal in this headless pipeline where the model IS the invoker. Flipped so prompt-encouraged stages can actually reach them via the Skill tool.

vendored.notes: MIT (LICENSE copied to plugin root). 7 of ~25 skills vendored: the requested grill-me, grill-with-docs, diagnosing-bugs, improve-codebase-architecture PLUS the three support skills their own SKILL.md bodies invoke via the Skill tool (grilling, domain-modeling, codebase-design) -- vendoring the four without the three would leave dangling Skill calls. diagnosing-bugs/scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh, improve-codebase-architecture/HTML-REPORT.md, domain-modeling/{ADR,CONTEXT}-FORMAT.md, codebase-design/{DEEPENING,DESIGN-IT-TWICE}.md kept -- all referenced from their own SKILL.md. All prompt-ENCOURAGED (not gate-required) initially; promotion to REQUIRED_SKILLS_BY_STAGE is telemetry-driven from persisted skills evidence.

skipped.name: security-guidance
skipped.reason: Hooks-ONLY plugin (no skills/commands/agents). Its SessionStart hook (ensure_agent_sdk.py) pip-installs claude-agent-sdk into a venv at session runtime -- a network fetch inside the sandbox, which must stay network-independent (it runs untrusted repos). Its UserPromptSubmit/PostToolUse/Stop hooks use asyncRewake background-rewake semantics that are undefined under this pipeline's per-turn headless `claude -p` runner. Stripping hooks (the impeccable precedent for unvalidated mechanisms) would leave an empty plugin. Security coverage already exists: the vendored security-review skill, the CLI's built-in security-review skill, and the deterministic semgrep/gitleaks/trivy/osv scan gates feeding remediation.

skipped.name: tdd (mattpocock/skills)
skipped.reason: Duplicates superpowers' test-driven-development, which is already REQUIRED at ac-to-tests and enforced by the skill gate. Requiring or even loading both invites a duplicate-methodology invocation with no added signal. Superpowers' version kept (user decision 2026-08-24).

skipped.name: to-spec (mattpocock/skills)
skipped.reason: Publishes the synthesized spec to an issue tracker (gh) -- no network/auth in the sandbox -- and duplicates this pipeline's own specification stage + spec ledger machinery. Its conversation-to-spec synthesis discipline was folded into agent/src/prompts/specification_draft.md instead (user decision 2026-08-24).

skipped.name: MCP-server plugins: context7, playwright, chrome-devtools-mcp, github, mintlify
skipped.reason: All are MCP servers needing runtime network and/or auth (context7 API, GitHub API, live browser control). Sandbox sessions are network-independent by design; the @playwright/mcp server was previously REMOVED from this image deliberately (see Dockerfile's PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION header). Lighthouse/a11y needs are met by the lighthouse CLI baked into the image and driven deterministically from e2e_nodes.py -- no MCP required.

skipped.name: claude-code-setup, plugin-dev, skill-creator
skipped.reason: Meta/authoring plugins (setup recommendations, plugin/skill development) with no role in a pipeline session. plugin-dev and skill-creator were explicitly excluded by the user (crossed out in the requesting screenshot).
